mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY growth exceeds 2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% MoM, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST declines by more than 10% YoY, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets due to lower borrowing costs, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases over three consecutive months, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases simultaneously, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% YoY signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where RSAFS grows by more than 2% YoY, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single meeting signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in one meeting, this hypothesis is rejected.
